subject: Offset time formats
notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically, all four normative sentences separately: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A zero to indicate that offset from UTC was not available on the system on which the information was recorded' -> OK (marker '3)'); 'If the data contains a zero in that character position, the offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields of the data shall both contain zero' -> OK; 'If the values contained in offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields of data in a receiving field associated with an offset subformat are both zero, the position corresponding to the plus sign in the format shall contain a plus sign' -> OK; 'The colon character in the offset subformat of an extended offset time format appears in the data associated with the format' -> OK. This is a COMPOUND rule with FOUR normative obligations plus three informative NOTEs; I located and read the implementation of every one. (a) '0' IS A PERMITTED SIGN VALUE. CobolDate.cs#Analyze lines 510-516: 'if (s.Field == Fld.OffSign) { ... char c = data[pos]; if (c is not ('+' or '-')) { if (c == '0') offZero = true; else return pos + 1; } pos++; continue; }' -- exactly the three values rules 1-3 enumerate are admitted and every other character yields the 1-based error position §15.92.4 requires. (b) A '0' SIGN FORCES BOTH SUBFIELDS TO ZERO. Analyze line 531: 'if (offZero && s.Field is Fld.OffHour or Fld.OffMinute) hi = 0;' collapses the §15.3.3.6.2 ranges (0..23 hours, 0..59 minutes) to the single value 0 for both, and the offZero flag is set before either is read because §15.3.3.6.1 puts the sign first in the subformat. Traced the per-digit narrowing at lines 543-548 by hand: sign '0' with hours '05' errors at the SECOND hours digit (the leading '0' is still consistent with the only legal '00'), which is the earliest character at which the error is determinable -- the §15.92.4 contract, not an off-by-one. (c) THE RECEIVING-FIELD REQUIREMENT ('+' when both subfields are zero). CobolDate.cs#EmitFormatted line 363 'osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'' can never produce '0' at all, and yields '+' at offsetMinutes == 0; lines 361-362 make oh/om zero only when offsetMinutes is exactly 0 (|offset| in 1..59 gives om != 0, >= 60 gives oh != 0), so the '-'-with-+0000 counterexample is unreachable. Verified by golden: conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/pb11_datetime_format_grammar 'OMIT-OFF=010000+0000' for FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm" 3600) with argument-3 omitted (§15.41.3 r6 evaluates it as 0) -- literally NOTE 3's '+0000'. (d) THE COLON OF AN EXTENDED OFFSET SUBFORMAT APPEARS IN THE DATA. CobolDate.cs#Tokenize line 277 emits Seg(IsField:false, Sep:':', InData:true); EmitFormatted line 369 'if (!s.IsField) { if (s.InData) sb.Append(s.Sep); continue; }' writes it, and Analyze lines 504-508 REQUIRE it in the data ('if (pos >= data.Length || data[pos] != s.Sep) return pos + 1'). Verified by golden: pb11 'T-OFF=01:00:00+01:00'. The bind-time recognizer agrees on the subformat's two shapes -- DateTimeFormatGrammar.cs#ZoneOfWidth lines 119-122 accept the five-character '+hhmm' and six-character '+hh:mm' and require the offset's width to MATCH the common part's, so a basic/extended chimera never reaches the runtime. Also confirmed the FORMAT always carries '+' as the placeholder and never a '-': Tokenize's '-' arm (line 276) does not set afterOffSign, so a hyphen is only ever the extended-date separator -- the format/data asymmetry these three rules describe is modelled correctly rather than collapsed. HONEST RESIDUE (why this row stays test-needed even at CONFORMS): obligations (a) and (b) -- the SENDING-field permission to write '0' with zero magnitude, and its rejection when the magnitude is non-zero -- are verified by implementation reading ONLY. No golden in tests/conformance/ feeds a '0' into an offset sign position; pb23 exercises the consuming path with '+' ('19950215T05142781+0500', the D.31.5.8/D.31.5.9 examples) and pb11 pins the producing path, so the cited tests close (c) and (d) but not (a)/(b). A closing golden would be TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("hhmmss+hhmm", "01000000000") = 0 with the non-zero-magnitude mate asserting the error position. NOTE 2's cross-reference to CURRENT-DATE / WHEN-COMPILED is informative and lands outside this clause: CobolDate.cs#Format21 renders §15.21.3's separate 21-character layout, whose position 17 is '0' only when the system lacks the local-time-differential facility -- .NET's DateTimeOffset always has one, so '+'/'-' is always correct there. Editions rationale identical to GR-15.3.3.6.1-1. || REFUTED: verdict CONFIRMED at CONFORMS after an independent re-derivation and a hand-trace of every branch; the record is changed to record what the note over-claimed and what residue remains. (1) ALL FOUR CITATIONS RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY and all return OK on §15.3.3.6.1 marker '3)'. Reading the clause whole shows FIVE normative sentences, not four: the note folds the SENDING-field permission ('For offset-time values used as sending fields, the position ... may contain a zero provided that ...' -- --check OK) into obligation (a) rather than naming it. It is nonetheless implemented by the same Analyze line 514 arm, so the omission is a labelling one. (2) OBLIGATION (b) HAND-TRACED, NOT ACCEPTED: with sign '0' Analyze line 531 forces hi = 0 while lo stays 0 for both Fld.OffHour (0,23) and Fld.OffMinute (0,59), and the per-digit narrowing at 543-548 then admits '00' and rejects everything else at the earliest determinable character -- I walked '01000000000' (accepted, returns 0), '0'+hours '01' (error at the SECOND hours digit, data position 9) and '0'+minutes '10' (error at the FIRST minute digit, position 10), all of which match §15.92.4's 'first position at which the error can be determined'. The hi=0 override is correctly scoped to OffHour/OffMinute and does NOT touch Fld.Minute, which shares the same (0,59) tuple -- the obvious way to get this wrong, checked. (3) THE FORMAT/DATA ASYMMETRY VERIFIED AT BOTH STAGES: DateTimeFormatGrammar.ZoneOfWidth lines 115-123 requires the offset subformat's width to match the common part's, and I confirmed by hand that both chimeras are rejected ('hhmmss+hh:mm' fails IsCommonTime at the extended width, 'hhmmssZ+hhmm' fails at both), and that FormatKindsAdmittedBy covers ALL SEVEN format-taking functions (IntrinsicBinder lines 382-392), so no function reaches CobolDate.Tokenize unscreened. (4) RESIDUE THE NOTE DID NOT DECLARE: obligation (d)'s CONSUMING side is also untested -- no fixture in tests/conformance feeds an extended '+hh:mm' offset into any analyzing function, so only the EMIT side of the colon rule is pinned (pb11 T-OFF); it rides the same 'if (data[pos] != s.Sep) return pos + 1' arm that the common-time colon exercises in conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/formatted_datetime, which is why the verdict holds on reading. (5) The code-location names Analyze, which houses only three of the five sentences -- the receiving-field '+' and the colon's emit half live in EmitFormatted/Tokenize; the single-path field forces the choice and Analyze is the right majority, but the row's code is genuinely three symbols in one file. (6) NOTE 2's CROSS-REFERENCE CHECKED RATHER THAN WAVED OFF: §15.21.3 position 17 does admit '0', CobolDate.Format21 line 35 never writes it, and that is correct because .NET always supplies the differential; but the SAME expression writes Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours) into positions 18-19, and .NET admits offsets to +14:00 while §15.21.3 caps the '+' case at 'the range 00 through 13' -- an out-of-subject divergence on RV-15.21.3-1, recorded here only because this clause's NOTE 2 is what points at it.
